sources.title: Visa Applications
sources.publisher: Embassy of the Kingdom of Lesotho in the United States of America
sources.officialityEvidence: This is the current official Lesotho Embassy in Washington website under the government .gov.ls domain. The page’s metadata shows modification on 11 March 2026 and it publishes a table headed “List of all countries” with incoming visa results and ordinary-passport processing.
sources.supportingExcerpt: YES – Citizens always require a Visa to enter Lesotho. NO – Citizens DO NOT require a Visa to enter Lesotho.

sources.title: E-Visa
sources.officialityEvidence: The current Ministry of Home Affairs page is the directly competent national immigration authority’s service page. It expressly reports the electronic visa system’s operational state and provides the official immigration email channel.
sources.supportingExcerpt: eVISA Applications System Suspended. Email: VISA-Applications.Immigration@gov.ls for online applications.

sources.title: Do I Need a Visa?
sources.officialityEvidence: This current Home Affairs immigration page asserts an eVisa-first rule but does not name its exemption countries. It is retained to make the direct conflict with the Ministry’s live suspension page explicit rather than treating online contact as an electronic visa issuance route.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Every citizen of a foreign country ... must first obtain a visa through the Lesotho e-visa system.

sources.title: Issuance of entry visa
sources.officialityEvidence: The central Government of Lesotho service charter publishes the tourist-entry-visa document requirements, fees and processing time; it is used only for scope conditions, not to expand the Embassy’s nationality table.
sources.supportingExcerpt: TOURIST – Application letter from the applicant ... Itinerary ... Passport copy ... Confirmation of hotel bookings/Accommodation.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: Lesotho visa-free short visit
policies.summary: Lesotho’s current Embassy table expressly marks these named passport nationalities “NO” for a visa. They therefore have a visa-free ordinary short-visitor route, subject to ordinary entry controls.
conditions: Applies only to the named foreign nationalities holding ordinary passports for the normal short-visitor baseline; the table does not state a stay duration for this non-asterisk cohort.

The table’s special passport fee rows and the separately described diplomatic, official/service, UN, laissez-passer, residence, work, business, transit, crew and special-document processes are not normalized into this policy.

Passport validity, any South African transit or re-entry document required by the journey, health requirements, funds, accommodation, onward travel, border inspection, security and individual admissibility remain applicable.

policies.title: Named ordinary passports: Lesotho visa-free visit up to 14 days
policies.summary: Lesotho’s current Embassy table marks these asterisked nationalities “NO” for a visa and explains that the asterisk requires a visa only for a stay exceeding 14 days.
conditions: Applies only to the named foreign ordinary passports for a visitor stay of no more than 14 days. The Embassy’s asterisk expressly requires a visa for a longer stay.
This is not evidence of residence, employment, study, business, transit, crew, diplomatic, official/service or special-document entry rights.

Passport validity, journey-specific South African transit or re-entry documentation, health, funds, accommodation, onward travel, border inspection, security and individual admissibility remain applicable.

policies.title: Other foreign ordinary passports: advance Lesotho visitor visa
policies.summary: The Embassy’s incoming table marks its listed remaining nationalities “YES” (visa always required), while Home Affairs supplies the explicit every-foreign-citizen visa default outside abolition and Commonwealth exemptions. The live eVisa service is suspended, so the current process is an advance email/manual visa workflow, not a nationality-wide eVisa or a walk-up arrival visa.
conditions: The Embassy states that applications are handled manually at Home Affairs or by email. Its published process says an approved applicant is sent a 72-hour “visa-on-arrival letter”; this pre-approval/entry letter does not establish a walk-up visa-on-arrival entitlement.

For current catalog issuers not printed as a distinct row in the Embassy’s legacy-named table, this policy relies on Home Affairs’ explicit rule that every foreign-country citizen needs a visa except the named abolition/Commonwealth exemptions; it is not inferred from table omission.
The Embassy says processing can take up to ten working days and limits entry under that letter to Maseru Port of Entry or Moshoeshoe I International Airport.

The Government service charter lists tourist application, itinerary, passport, accommodation, financial, medical-insurance and medical-report requirements; the Embassy additionally lists journey-specific South African transit or re-entry visa requirements for Bangladesh and Pakistan.

The Ministry’s current pages conflict: one retains eVisa-first wording, but its live eVisa service page expressly says the system is suspended. The current Embassy page describes manual/email processing, so email submission or an arrival letter is not normalized as eVisa. Residence, work, study, business, transit, crew, diplomatic, official/service, UN, laissez-passer and other special-document arrangements are excluded.
Every admission remains subject to fees, passport validity, health, funds, accommodation, onward travel, border inspection, security and individual admissibility.
